newsitem.title: EGYPT: Private sector to build cement plant in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Private sector to build cement plant in Egypt.

text.p: The private sector will build a cement plant in Egypt with total investment of 600 million pounds ($176 million), an official close to the project was quoted on Tuesday as saying.
"It is the first cement plant to be set up by the private sector,"Mohamed Mahmoud Hassan, chairman of the Egyptian Federation for Building and Construction, said in the daily al-Akhbar newspaper.
"The plant, which will have an annual capacity of 1.2 million tonnes, will cover demand in the southern provinces of Qena, Aswan and Red Sea," he added.
The venture will be set up in the city of Qeft, some 450 km(280 miles) south of Cairo, said Hassan, whose federation is among the founders. He did not say when building would begin.
A public offer to sell nine million shares, at 10.00 pounds ($3) each in Egypt Cement (Qena) will be open on February 16, the founders have said in a paid announcement.
The offer in the new venture will remain open for a month from February 16, but it could be closed after a minimum of ten days if it is fully covered, they added.
Investors can apply for 25 shares or more, with only a quarter of their value payable plus an issue fee of 0.10 pounds a share, the published prospectus said.
It added that another 25 percent of the share value is to be paid within six months of the date of establishment. The company will ask for the remaining half within a year.
State-owned banks and insurance firms, including the National Bank of Egypt, the agent of the offer, hold at least 40 percent of the firm, which has a paid up capital of 300 million pounds.
The expected annual return on capital would be 10 percent, the founders said.
The cement sector is highly profitable in Egypt and cement firms are among the stock market blue chips.
